meta_description: The sycamore at Brandywine, Bartram's Ginkgo in Philadelphia and the champion trees of Pittsburgh's Mellon Park. {trees} trees across {places} places.
intro: Pennsylvania's oldest trees have been standing through American history since before it had a name. At Chadds Ford a sycamore roughly four hundred years old was already mature when the Battle of Brandywine broke around it in 1777, beside a house the wounded were carried into. In Philadelphia, a ginkgo at Bartram's Garden is one of three saplings shipped from London in 1785, the first of their species to reach North America. Pittsburgh keeps its remarkable trees in parks rather than on streets: in Mellon Park a bald cypress grows far from any swamp, a katsura smells of burnt sugar every autumn, and a lacebark pine sheds its bark in patches. The city also names Giving Trees, chosen for what they do for everything living around them rather than for how big they are.
